title: Deception Island 1965: The Antarctic UFO Incident Documented by the Argentine Navy
excerpt: Seventeen military witnesses, theodolite trajectory tracking, and simultaneous geomagnetic instrument anomalies during the 1965 Antarctica UAP sighting.
content:
Seventeen military witnesses, theodolite trajectory tracking, and simultaneous geomagnetic instrument anomalies during the 1965 Antarctica UAP sighting.

• November 16, 2026

In 20 seconds: In July 1965, seventeen military personnel stationed at the remote volcanic caldera of Deception Island in Antarctica observed a silent, lens-shaped luminous craft performing impossible aerodynamic maneuvers over twenty minutes. Tracked by meteorological theodolites and accompanied by violent electromagnetic perturbations on base magnetometers, the incident led the Argentine Navy to issue an unprecedented official press release acknowledging an authentic unidentified aerial phenomenon.

  • Multi-National Observation: Simultaneous sightings documented across three separate national bases: Argentina (Deception Detachment), Chile (Aguirre Cerda Base), and the United Kingdom (British Antarctic Survey).
  • Instrumental Verification: Trajectory plotted via scientific optical theodolite while geomagnetic variographs detected synchronous electromagnetic anomalies.
  • Official Navy Communique: On July 7, 1965, the Argentine Navy publicly confirmed the reality of the sighting, ruling out aircraft, satellites, and atmospheric weather balloons.

The Polar Winter of 1965

Located in the South Shetland archipelago, Deception Island is a breached volcanic caldera that forms one of the safest natural harbors in Antarctica. In the heart of the southern polar winter of 1965, the island was home to research stations operated by Argentina, Chile, and the United Kingdom.

On the evening of July 3, 1965, at 19:42 local time, sub-zero temperatures and pitch darkness enveloped the Argentine Naval Detachment. Corporal First Class Ramón Galván was stepping outside to take meteorological readings when an anomalous light captured his attention above Mount Kirkwood.

Galván immediately alerted the detachment commander, Lieutenant Daniel Perissé. Within minutes, seventeen military personnel, including meteorologists and radio operators, stood outside observing the object.

The Theodolite and the Magnetometer

What sets the Deception Island case apart from standard folklore is the presence of scientific instrumentation operated by trained military technicians.

As the object hovered and altered its coloration from vivid red to emerald green and brilliant white, base personnel aligned a precision meteorological theodolite—an instrument normally utilized to track high-altitude weather balloons. The theodolite allowed observers to calculate the object’s elevation angle at 45 degrees and determine that its apparent diameter exceeded that of a full moon.

Simultaneously, in the geomagnetic recording hut, the base’s variographic magnetometers began registering anomalous spikes. The instrument, designed to measure terrestrial magnetic field fluctuations, recorded severe disturbances matching the exact entry, hover, and exit timestamps of the craft.

The Official Argentine Navy Statement

Following a radio transmission from Lieutenant Perissé to naval headquarters in Buenos Aires, military leadership took the rare step of verifying the testimonies through cross-checks with the Chilean and British commanders.

On July 7, 1965, the Secretariat of the Argentine Navy issued an official communique published across international news wires:

“The naval detachment on Deception Island observed on July 3 a luminous object, lens-shaped, which moved on an oscillating trajectory toward the northeast. The phenomenon was witnessed by the entire personnel of the base and coincided with disturbances in the local magnetic field recorded by the detachment’s instruments.”

The Chilean Air Force subsequently corroborated the event, confirming that their personnel at Aguirre Cerda Base had witnessed identical maneuvers over twenty minutes.

Sixty years later, the Deception Island incident remains one of the most thoroughly documented multi-witness military UAP encounters in modern history.

Frequently Asked Questions

What was the 1965 Deception Island UFO incident?

It was a series of multi-witness unidentified flying object sightings recorded in June and July 1965 over Deception Island and the Antarctic Peninsula by personnel from Argentine, Chilean, and British military research bases, culminating in an official communique issued by the Argentine Secretariat of the Navy.

Who was Lieutenant Commander Daniel Perissé?

Daniel Perissé was the Argentine naval officer commanding the Deception Island Naval Detachment in 1965. A trained military observer, he documented the optical characteristics, duration, and theodolite trajectory measurements of the craft, later rising to the rank of Frigate Captain.

What instrumental evidence was recorded during the sighting?

Beyond seventeen direct human eyewitnesses, meteorological personnel used an optical theodolite to track the object's elevation and heading. Simultaneously, the base's variographic magnetometers registered sharp electromagnetic fluctuations as the object passed overhead.

Did Chile and the United Kingdom also report the object?

Yes. Personnel at the Chilean Base Presidente Pedro Aguirre Cerda on Deception Island and scientists at the British Antarctic Survey station reported identical aerial phenomena maneuvering silently on the exact same dates.
